title: Crossing the Fold or Renting the Lira? Currency Choice as an Evolutionary Coordination Game and the Full Cycle of Türkiye's FX-Protected Deposits
content: Deposit dollarisation exposes banks, borrowers and the public budget to currency risk, and programmes that subsidise saving in the domestic currency transfer that risk to the state. Does such a subsidy move savers across a coordination threshold, or merely rent their loyalty while it lasts? This paper models deposit denomination as an evolutionary coordination game with network externalities and shows that the replicator-mutator dynamic is a gradient system whose fold bifurcations have closed forms. Hysteresis exists if and only if the bistability index s = λβ/μ exceeds four, and the loop width grows as (s − 4)3/2 near the cusp. A subsidy produces a permanent switch only if it exceeds the fold gap and outlasts a minimal duration that diverges as the inverse square root of the excess dose; the cheapest sufficient programme is the largest and shortest. An exact identity separates valuation, accrual and switching in the dollarisation ratio. Applied to Türkiye’s foreign-exchange-protected (FX-protected) deposits (2021–2025), the geometry implies that the pre-programme and post-exit shares can both be rest points only if s is at most about 4.8, so that any memory created by the scheme is thin, and it yields a falsifiable criterion for reversal risk.
